templates.text: The auditory pathways are severely underdeveloped, failing to process even the loudest environmental sounds.
Severe auditory channel deficiency results in a profound lack of startle response to acoustic stimuli.
Auditory processing is critically impaired, with neural signals from the cochlea failing to reach the brainstem.
The infant's auditory system exhibits a profound deficit, showing no orienting behavior towards any sound source.
A severe underdevelopment of the auditory nerve leads to an effective absence of functional hearing.
Critical malformation of the inner ear structures renders the auditory channel non-functional.
The auditory cortex shows minimal activity, unable to interpret any incoming sound signals.
There is a profound bilateral auditory deficit, with no evidence of sound localization or discrimination.
Neural transmission along the auditory pathway is severely disrupted, preventing perception of voice or noise.
The cochlea and auditory nerve complex are severely dysplastic, creating a complete sensory block.
Auditory input is met with a {delay}-second neural processing delay before any faint cortical registration.
A profound auditory agnosia is present; the brain cannot recognize any sound as meaningful.
The infant demonstrates no auditory blink reflex, even to sudden, high-intensity sounds exceeding {db} dB.
Severe hypoplasia of the auditory brainstem nuclei critically impairs all sound processing.
The auditory system is functionally isolated, with sensory input failing to integrate into higher networks.
A profound conductive and sensorineural auditory deficit prevents any airborne sound perception.
Critical failure in auditory pathway myelination results in absent acoustic evoked potentials.
The infant's auditory threshold is profoundly elevated, perceiving only extreme low-frequency vibration.
Auditory channel development arrested, leaving only rudimentary brainstem responses to intense stimuli.
A severe bilateral auditory neuropathy disrupts synchronization of neural firing necessary for hearing.
The auditory cortex lacks the tonotopic organization required to decode frequency or pitch.
Profound auditory deprivation is evident due to non-patent neural pathways from the ear.
The infant shows no auditory habituation, as repeated sounds never register to begin with.
A critical deficit in the auditory midbrain colliculi prevents any orienting to sound.
The auditory system is severely underdeveloped, with hair cell function and neural transmission both absent.
Auditory processing is so severely impaired that the infant does not react to its own cry.
A profound sensorineural auditory loss stems from malformed cochlear hair cells and ganglion cells.
The auditory nerve shows minimal electrophysiological activity, indicating a severe functional deficit.
Critical auditory pathway dysgenesis results in an inability to process temporal or spectral sound features.
The infant's auditory world is silent due to a severe, bilateral disruption of the central auditory pathway.
